title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
A man used AI image generation to create explicit synthetic images of a woman he knew from college, then distributed them through multiple fake social media accounts and email addresses. The abuse was a form of non-consensual intimate imagery enabled by the ease of the technology and the use of anonymization to evade detection. The system deployment—an AI image generator available to create these images—had no guardrails preventing their creation or any human review of the use case.

The failure was caught only after the victim discovered the content circulating and reported it to police, who traced the perpetrator through digital forensics. A technical barrier at the point of generation, such as refusing to create explicit images from identifiable faces, could have prevented the harm upstream. The deployment of generative AI without such safeguards placed the burden of protection on law enforcement rather than on the system itself.

It is not established whether Bansal used a commercial image generation service, an open-source tool, or another platform, or what security measures, if any, were in place.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and sharing obscene AI-generated images of a college acquaintance. Bansal allegedly obtained photographs from the woman's private social media account and used artificial intelligence technology to generate explicit morphed images. He then distributed this content through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook while using various Gmail addresses to hide his identity.

The victim, also 22 years old, reported the harassment to the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi after receiving messages from anonymous accounts informing her that her manipulated photographs and videos were circulating online. During the investigation, police analyzed digital evidence including social media accounts and email records to trace the perpetrator. Bansal admitted during questioning that he knew the woman from college and had developed personal resentment toward her. Police recovered his mobile phone, two SIM cards, and other digital evidence. The investigation is continuing.
